subject: QMAN_V3_DIRECTPATH_PORTABLE_IMPLEMENTATION
purpose: A target-repository-independent implementation contract for VMware-aligned Static, Dynamic, managed-owner, lifecycle, and dual-online-host cold-relocation behavior.

normativeSourceClosureRule.GIT_BLOB_BYTES: SHA-256 of exact repository LF bytes, rendered sha256:<64 lowercase hex>. Symlinks, path traversal, missing files, and working-tree bytes that differ from the pinned target blob fail closed.
normativeSourceClosureRule.REPOSITORY_TREE_V1: Recursively include every regular file below the named tree root, including hidden files, without following symlinks; submodules and .git entries are forbidden. Preserve exact case, use NFC UTF-8 tree-root-relative POSIX paths (for acceptance/cases this is C10.json, not acceptance/cases/C10.json), and reject NFC/case-fold collisions so Windows and Linux enumerate the same set. Encode each file as the closed object {path,sha256}, where sha256 covers exact raw LF bytes; sort records by the CANONICAL-JSON-V1 bytes of path; hash the CANONICAL-JSON-V1 array of records. The object framing makes path/content boundaries unambiguous.
normativeSourceClosureRule.closureAuthority: The portable contract's own CANONICAL-JSON-V1 hash transitively binds this complete closure. A changed design, policy, wire schema, mapping schema, or Case tree invalidates sourceContract.sha256 and every downstream scenario/map approval.

sourcePrecedence: Accepted product decisions and compatibility policy define product scope.
This contract defines portable interfaces, state, concurrency, reasons, and handoff obligations.
The normative design and implementation blueprint define algorithms and evidence detail not repeated here.

A target integration map may bind symbols but may not weaken a fail-closed invariant.

portableSpecification.doesNotProve: Any private Qman symbol exists, any product code is implemented, or any platform/device profile is qualified.

targetCodeMapping.doesNotProve: Implementation correctness or qualification merely because names are mapped.

implementationBoundary.combinationConstraint: A target may co-locate ports in one process, but authority, transaction boundaries, stable reasons, and negative gates remain distinguishable and testable.
minimumAuthorityRules: Only the global repository decides bundle lease ownership, assignedId lifetime, run generation, and host epoch.
Only the host agent performs driver bind, reset, backend-grant creation, attach verification, and teardown side effects.
The local journal cannot arbitrate cross-host ownership and TTL expiry cannot prove physical release.
The launcher cannot select a Dynamic device or become the durable owner authority.
Raw QEMU, unrestricted QMP, sysfs, and unmanaged VFIO entry points cannot bypass admission or lifecycle gates.

profiles.standard: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) with the additional schema restrictions below
rules: Object property names are sorted by their UTF-16 code units exactly as RFC 8785 requires.
Schema-constrained text inputs must already be Unicode NFC; validation rejects non-NFC input and the canonicalizer never normalizes or otherwise changes parsed strings.
String escaping and literal serialization follow RFC 8785 without ASCII-only escaping.

Integers use minimal base-10 notation and every JSON numeric integer is restricted to the inclusive interoperable range -9007199254740991..9007199254740991; unsigned counters therefore use 0..9007199254740991. Values needing a wider domain are schema-defined canonical decimal strings, never JSON numbers. Floating-point values are forbidden in identity, CAS, plan, manifest, receipt, and evidence-hash inputs.
Arrays retain semantic order; set-valued arrays are deduplicated and sorted by their element canonical bytes before hashing.
No insignificant whitespace is emitted.
An omitted optional field and an explicit null are distinct and schemas state which is legal.
Hexadecimal IDs and digests use lowercase; a digest string includes its algorithm prefix.
profiles.hashForm: sha256 of the exact canonical UTF-8 bytes, rendered as sha256:<64 lowercase hex digits>
profiles.integerEnforcement: Closed JSON Schema validation plus tools/validate_portable_handoff.py recursively rejects every JSON numeric integer outside this range before canonicalization, hashing, signature verification, CAS comparison, or persistence.
profiles.compatibility: A producer writes only V1 until a separately versioned canonical profile and dual-read migration are accepted.

profiles.meaning: UTC RFC 3339 with exactly six fractional digits and literal Z; offsets, leap-second spelling, omitted fractions, and variable precision are rejected before hashing.

rules: BDF is only a current locator and is re-resolved from deviceUid under a pinned snapshot.

STRONG_SERIAL uses only the closed provider/version branches PCI_DSN_EUI64_V1, PCI_VPD_SN_UTF8_V1, or VENDOR_QUALIFIED_BYTES_V1. Exact provider descriptor, extraction material, endianness/normalization and domain-separated serialValueHash all enter the fingerprint; raw serial bytes never enter normal logs.
pciIds.classCode and the exact CLASS_CODE_ROLE_V1-derived functionRole enter the fingerprint; an arbitrary role label is invalid.

Without a qualified serial provider, SLOT_BOUND requires one closed provider/version ACPI_FIRMWARE_PATH_V1, SMBIOS_SYSTEM_SLOT_V1, or DEVICETREE_FULL_PATH_V1 and its grammar-valid path. BDF, sysfs, VFIO minor and IOMMU-group aliases are invalid; no stable path means the device is not a Static target.
SLOT_BOUND Static is disabled unless the exact compatibility profile explicitly allows it and an administrator enrolls the device; Dynamic may use it as a host-local identity.
A changed fingerprint creates a different identity and invalidates Static backing, pending owner intent, plan, lease authorization, and clean-release matching.
Static additionally pins expected physical path and current BDF and requires explicit re-enrollment when either locator changes, even when a STRONG_SERIAL fingerprint is unchanged.
Cross-host Dynamic equivalence never means identity equality; the target solver chooses a new local deviceUid.

profiles.signatureEncoding: ed25519:<unpadded base64url of exactly 64 signature bytes>
profiles.projectionRule: Deep-copy the complete closed-schema document; set its exact signature field to null and its exact digest field to null; retain every other present field unchanged; reject floats, duplicate keys, non-NFC strings, unknown fields, and integers outside the interoperable range; encode the projection with RFC 8785 CANONICAL-JSON-V1.
profiles.digestRule: documentDigest = SHA-256(canonical UTF-8 projection bytes). The stored subject-specific digest field must equal documentDigest.
profiles.preimageRule: Ed25519 signs ASCII(domainSeparator) || single 0x00 byte || canonical UTF-8 projection bytes. The signature field itself and digest field are therefore unambiguously excluded while signer, role, key-ring version, validity, evidence hashes, and all payload fields remain covered.

profiles.trustRule: Resolve signerKeyId/keyId in ENTITY-TRUST-KEY-RING at the signed issued/decided time; require exact role, Ed25519 public key, validity window, non-revocation, a complete genesis-to-current TrustKeyRingHistory with no sequence/digest/identity discontinuity, independently supplied external rollback-anchor state, a verifier-nonce live AnchorFreshnessEnvelope, and root signatures chaining to the out-of-band CONFIG-TRUST-ROOT-DIGEST. A trust root, history, nonce or rollback anchor supplied only by the integration map/target/evidence artifact cannot authenticate that same artifact. Unknown, expired, revoked, rolled-back, stale, self-bootstrapped, role-mismatched, or unverifiable keys fail closed.
profiles.separationOfDutiesRule: Qualification Engineering and Product Release use distinct keyIds, Ed25519 public-key material and immutable principalIds; TARGET_ARCHITECT, SECURITY, and TEST map approvals use three distinct keyIds, public keys and principalIds. approval.identity byte-equals the resolved key principalId. One principal or trust-ring key cannot carry incompatible approval roles, and PRODUCT_RELEASE approval remains a separately attributable act.
profiles.keyRingRootRule: For ENTITY-TRUST-KEY-RING, deep-copy the complete ring, set rootSignatures to an empty array and keyRingDigest to null, then apply CANONICAL-JSON-V1. keyRingDigest is SHA-256 of those bytes. Each root signature signs ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/TRUST-KEY-RING/V1) || 0x00 || CANONICAL-JSON-V1({rootKeyId,signedAt,keyRingDigest}), so signedAt remains covered. Accept the ring only when the configured offline root set whose digest equals CONFIG-TRUST-ROOT-DIGEST verifies the required distinct-principal quorum, the complete history resolves previousKeyRingDigest to genesis, and the live external rollback anchor/freshness response confirms current keyRingSequence/keyRingDigest.

canonicalizationContract.hashSubjectRule: Every schemaRef is a closed normative projection. Target storage may add local columns outside these descriptors, but cross-port messages, CAS compare values, signatures, plan/launch authorization and audit references use only the declared canonical descriptor/digest. A target IDL binding must preserve names, types, nullability and set/order semantics or report CONFLICT.

safetyGuards.rule: The exact typed operation lease commits under global CAS before the first owner, driver, reset, VFIO, QEMU, or cleanup side effect; a lease of another type never authorizes the action.
safetyGuards.ownerTransitionRule: OWNER_TRANSITION is acquired for the complete ownerActivationGroup before any member is unbound or rebound.
safetyGuards.failureRule: Lease acquisition conflict produces no host side effect; loss or ambiguity after a side effect enters reconcile and retains/quarantines the complete scope.
safetyGuards.executorValidationRule: Every side-effecting port receives and validates the sealed typed operation capability {operationLeaseId, leaseType, scopeHash, holderControllerGeneration, operationLeaseResourceVersion}; it must match the live global row, exact run/intent and local journal scope before each first/non-idempotent side effect. A BundleLease ID, maintenance token, caller role, or raw controller request is never a substitute.

safetyGuards.name: ReleaseOwnershipGuard
safetyGuards.acquireRule: Before requesting QEMU stop or performing any release/rollback side effect, the Host Agent atomically acquires one RELEASE typed operation lease and one ReleaseOwnershipGuard for the complete assignment lease/bundle set; every existing assignment claim remains pinned until one all-or-nothing clean-release or quarantine commit.
safetyGuards.preSpawnRule: qemuPidStarttimeOrNull is null only when the fsynced launch journal and process census prove that no managed QEMU was ever created for this run generation; otherwise the exact pid/starttime is mandatory before stop or teardown.
safetyGuards.fdLifetimeRule: No QEMU-owned VFIO group, device, container, cdev, or IOMMUFD descriptor is duplicated or deliberately retained in another process beyond the QEMU process lifetime merely to make release easier.
safetyGuards.contextRule: The guard first revokes every new launch/open entry point. After exact QEMU pid/starttime exit and descriptor teardown are proven, or never-created proof is accepted, the Host Agent re-resolves every IDENTITY-V1 member under the current host epoch and reacquires the minimum backend-specific release contexts authorized by the original lease set and profile; Legacy reopens exact group/device paths, while future cdev/IOMMUFD follows its independently qualified reopen/detach contract.
safetyGuards.exclusionRule: The guard excludes new attach, owner transition, reset by another run, relocation target use, and quarantine clear until clean-release CAS or quarantine commit.
safetyGuards.receiptRule: Reacquired context identity, ioctl sequence, descriptor close, DMA/IRQ teardown, IOMMU invalidate, reset/state probe, owner restore, and guard release are typed receipt fields.
safetyGuards.failureRule: Failure to acquire the full-scope guard, re-resolve identity, reacquire any context, or prove any cleanup step retains every logical claim and quarantines the complete affected assignment scope.

dynamicCandidateEquivalence.rule: Two candidates are substitutable for one Dynamic requirement only when every signature field is equal under the request's equivalence policy and both independently pass current capability and availability.
dynamicCandidateEquivalence.bundleIdRule: bundleId deduplicates or excludes overlapping physical candidates on one host; equality or inequality of bundleId alone never proves semantic equivalence.
dynamicCandidateEquivalence.multiRequirementRule: The solver evaluates equivalence and nonoverlap across the complete requirement set and guest resource plan, then atomically reserves the selected bundles.
dynamicCandidateEquivalence.relocationRule: A target candidate receives a new target-local identity and assignedId but must preserve the required equivalence signature, profile, and guest ABI.

canonicalSelectionContract.comparisonEncoding: Every scalar comparison uses its CANONICAL-JSON-V1 element bytes; integers compare numerically before text components; digests include the lowercase sha256: prefix. No locale, database collation, BDF enumeration, map insertion order, random seed, or wall-clock time participates.

candidatePreferenceKey.definition: Count the exact optional selector dimensions constrained and matched by the chosen AllowedDevice tuple among subsystemVendorId, subsystemDeviceId, and revisionId, then add one when the requirement has an exact customLabel. If several AllowedDevice tuples match one candidate, use the lexicographically greatest [specificity, tuple canonical bytes] pair before forming this count.
LOCAL=0, UNKNOWN=1, REMOTE=2; a strict-local policy removes UNKNOWN and REMOTE before scoring.
Four non-negative integer components in bytes/count: [below4GBytes, highMmioBytes, bridgeWindowBytes, virtualSlotCost].
Canonical non-empty deviceUid set, sorted by CANONICAL-JSON-V1 element bytes.

canonicalSelectionContract.solutionScore: Order selected bindings by expandedSlotIdentity ascending, concatenate each complete candidatePreferenceKey in that order, then append the exact plan waste tuple [below4GBytes, highMmioBytes, bridgeWindowBytes, virtualSlotCost]. Choose the lexicographically smallest complete score.
canonicalSelectionContract.completeSearchRule: Search all feasible complete solutions within the pinned deterministic solver bound. Candidate/search order is only a traversal hint. Never return the first complete or greedy solution. TIMEOUT is a stable non-retryable denial with no partial result or reservation.
canonicalSelectionContract.tieRule: Two solutions are canonically identical only when the complete solutionScore bytes are identical; otherwise exactly one is preferred. The selected score and solver-bound/profile hash enter decisionHash and evidence.

dataEntities.immutability: Every global mutation compares controllerGeneration and resourceVersion. Expiry fences a controller from new mutations but never releases a physical device claim.
Boot or agent-authority replacement increments hostEpoch/generation. ONLINE or heartbeat state is scheduling evidence only and never proves physical clean release.

Content is immutable and signed by HOST_INVENTORY_EVIDENCE authority; a changed observation creates a new epoch. Publication atomically advances ENTITY-HOST-AUTHORITY's current snapshot pointer, and an older correctly signed snapshot cannot authorize new planning or side effects.
deviceUid binds immutable identity; BDF is a locator and never identity.

Append-only CANONICAL-JSON-V1 key ring. keyRingDigest hashes keyId, immutable principalId, public-key material, roles and validity with rootSignatures excluded by the separately provisioned root-envelope verifier; sequence/previous digest and an external rollback anchor prevent rollback. Reassigning a key/public key to another principal is invalid and rotation creates a new keyId. Root public keys are not stored as trust merely because they appear in this ring; their exact digest is pinned by CONFIG-TRUST-ROOT-DIGEST.

Qualification Engineering signs CANONICAL-JSON-V1 bytes with Ed25519; any exact key, dependency, validity, Case, evidence, signer, or signature change creates a new record digest and never edits an approved record in place.

Product Release signs an append-only CANONICAL-JSON-V1 catalog with Ed25519. Sequence and previous digest are monotonic and checked against an external rollback anchor; revocation and key rotation create a new catalog and invalidate new admission under older state.

This is a resolved read model. Any dependency, qualification record, catalog sequence, revocation, key-ring, or policy change creates a new profile hash and invalidates dependent plan/launch authorization.
Each accepted mutation creates a new requestVersion over CANONICAL-JSON-V1 bytes; an execution run references one exact request hash and version.
The bundle is a closure for one snapshot; changed membership invalidates the plan.
The independent Owner FSM transitions by CAS; pending reboot never retargets an identity by VID:DID, and a new attempt receives a new run identity.
A new execution attempt receives a new run generation; stale generations cannot mutate it.
A binding is reserved and committed only with the complete run. Device, bundle, guest slot, generation, or assignedId changes create a new run generation rather than retargeting the row.
One atomic lease covers the full exclusive attach group; TTL is liveness metadata only.

dataEntities.multiBindingRule: Version 2 has one ordered binding per Static request member or Dynamic requirement result; the manifest-level plan proves their complete nonoverlap and atomic commit.
dataEntities.compatibility: A V1 single-binding manifest may be read and normalized to one V2 binding, but every new write is V2 and no V2 multi-binding manifest is down-converted.
dataEntities.immutability: Append-only audit record encoded with CANONICAL-JSON-V1; never substitutes for the live lease authority.
The Host Agent SQLite journal is an append-only fsynced hash chain of INTENT, RESULT, and COMPENSATION entries. It is recovery evidence/cache and never global ownership authority.

The Ed25519-signed CANONICAL-JSON-V1 receipt is immutable, nonce-bound, full-assignment-scope, source-epoch-bound, and accepted exactly once by one CAS against the complete old lease set; that acceptance creates a durable source-clean fact which serial target attempts may reference without re-consuming or weakening the receipt.

Append-only global-repository fact created in the same serializable transaction that compares every old authority/lease version, consumes the unexpired full-scope receipt exactly once, revokes the complete lease set, advances the authority resourceVersion, and writes audit/outbox rows. It is signed by CONTROL_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE; identical idempotent replay returns the same fact and any different receipt, scope, version, or generation is rejected.

This receipt is valid only before the first host-action INTENT. It permits one atomic cancellation of the complete unstarted reservation and cannot substitute for physical clean-release after any owner/reset/VFIO/QEMU side effect.

Sticky fail-closed record for one canonical affected assignment/owner scope. All per-bundle rows, retained claims, and deny indexes are created or cleared in one global transaction; only audited full-scope remediation may clear it.
The independent remediation FSM advances by expected quarantine generation and resourceVersion; failure never clears or narrows the sticky quarantine scope.

Relocation has its own FSM and generation. Source and target Assignment runs remain separate aggregates. A source-clean receipt is accepted once into sourceCleanFactVersion; each target attempt has a new attempt/run identity and generation, is serialized in append-only audit history, and may not overwrite source state or reuse assignedId.
The same key and hash replay the same run/result; the same key with a different hash is rejected.
A typed lease authorizes exactly one operation kind and complete scope; changing type or scope requires a new CAS acquisition.

The guard is exclusive, exact-run and complete-assignment-scope; leaseBindings is the complete canonical leaseId/version/bundle set and qemuPidStarttime may be null only with a durable never-created launch proof. Only one atomic clean-release CAS or quarantine commit terminates it.
Append-only CANONICAL-JSON-V1 audit event; it records authority decisions and correlations but never substitutes for a lease, receipt, or evidence artifact.
Created in the same database transaction as the aggregate transition; delivery is at-least-once and consumers deduplicate by outboxId plus aggregateVersion.

transitionExecutionBindingContract.purpose: Prevent a target from satisfying a transition mapping with only one nearby symbol while inventing actor, ordering, transaction, journal, compensation, or crash-recovery semantics.
transitionExecutionBindingContract.orderedOperationRule: stateMachines[*].transitions[*].operationIds is normative order. Each operation's logical actor is its backendNeutralOperations.ownerPortId even when multiple ports are co-located in one private service.
transitionExecutionBindingContract.sideEffectRule: Before the first HOST_SIDE_EFFECT or EXTERNAL_PROCESS operation, the target binding identifies a durable typed operation lease and, where host action is possible, an fsynced ENTITY-HOST-ACTION-JOURNAL INTENT. Observations and receipts follow the side effect; the authoritative aggregate/outbox commit is last.
transitionExecutionBindingContract.transactionRule: Every transition mapping declares the exact same-transaction entity write set, compared version/generation fields, assignedId behavior, outbox events, and success state. Multi-aggregate release, rollback, quarantine, and relocation use OP-CAS-TRANSITION-AGGREGATES and cannot split the declared write set.
transitionExecutionBindingContract.failureRule: Every operationId/reasonCode failure point maps to a typed authoritative state, lease/claim/assignedId/release-guard effect, quarantine scope, retry policy, and compensation transition set. The union is exact and every failure point has an executable crash scenario. Unknown physical cleanup never maps to FREE.
transitionExecutionBindingContract.verificationRule: PRODUCT_IMPLEMENTED requires every BOUND TRANSITION item to carry this binding and an EXECUTED_PASS crash/concurrency scenario at the same target commit; the semantic evaluator recomputes operations, actors, states, reasons, hashes, and evidence.

casRules.invariant: A pre-reboot or pre-reconcile observation cannot authorize a current action.

reasonCodes.meaning: The exact planner reached its bounded search limit without a proof of satisfiability.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Tune and requalify planner limits; never fallback to greedy placement.

reasonCodes.meaning: No complete candidate solution meets the versioned NUMA policy.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Change placement or select a qualified policy/profile.

reasonCodes.meaning: A required guest BAR is zero or missing after launch.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Abort commit, cleanly rollback, and correct the guest resource profile.

reasonCodes.meaning: The selected backend/QEMU combination cannot express the planned topology.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Use or implement a separately qualified backend adapter/profile.

reasonCodes.meaning: The renderer cannot encode the planned MMIO aperture/floor for this profile.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Add an exact renderer capability and requalify it.

reasonCodes.meaning: The backend cannot honor the exact planned resource placement.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Reject the launch or use a qualified profile; do not let firmware improvise.

reasonCodes.meaning: Kernel/backend ioctl capability does not match the exact adapter profile.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Select a compatible kernel/QEMU/backend profile.

reasonCodes.meaning: Backend descriptors or attachments cannot be proven closed.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Retain the claim and quarantine if recovery cannot prove closure.

reasonCodes.meaning: The Host Agent cannot reacquire the exact qualified backend-specific cleanup context under ReleaseOwnershipGuard.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Retain the lease and guard claim, quarantine the complete bundle, and repair the adapter-specific recovery path.

reasonCodes.meaning: The exact RELEASE operation lease or ReleaseOwnershipGuard cannot be exclusively acquired for the complete bundle.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Do not touch backend or device state; reconcile the current guard/lease holder and quarantine on ambiguity.

reasonCodes.meaning: A Static deviceUid is unavailable on the requested target host.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Return to the original host or explicitly reconfigure the Static assignment.

reasonCodes.meaning: The managed QEMU process failed before verified ATTACHED commit.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Execute verified reverse cleanup or quarantine the complete bundle.

reasonCodes.meaning: The managed QEMU process exited unexpectedly.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Enter release/reconcile; never free from process absence alone.

reasonCodes.meaning: The exact QEMU pid/starttime exit cannot be proven.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Retain the claim until process identity and exit are resolved.

reasonCodes.meaning: DMA maps, IRQ routes, or IOMMU invalidation cannot be proven removed.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Retain and quarantine the complete bundle.

reasonCodes.meaning: The original host owner/provider cannot be proven restored where required.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Retain and quarantine the complete bundle.

reasonCodes.meaning: Observed topology, BAR, bridge window, firmware, identity, IRQ, or IOMMU state differs from the plan.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Abort commit, preserve evidence, and invalidate or correct the backend profile.

reasonCodes.meaning: A probe required by the production profile is absent or not bound to this guest boot.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Restore the required probe; a firmware-only profile cannot commit a production guest.

reasonCodes.meaning: Logical lease, local backend, process, or observed device owner facts disagree or are incomplete.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Retain all claims and reconcile; never select the most convenient source.

reasonCodes.meaning: At least one mandatory cleanup or restore proof is failed or unknown.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Quarantine the complete bundle and keep the lease/claim until audited remediation.

reasonCodes.meaning: No authoritative full-bundle source clean-release receipt gates the target handoff.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Keep the VM stopped and target unreserved; reconcile the source.

reasonCodes.meaning: The source receipt does not match the current source epoch, old lease version, run generation, or member set.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Reject it and obtain a new clean-release proof from the source.

reasonCodes.meaning: A required online cooperative host cannot complete the current handshake or source cleanup.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Keep the VM stopped, retain the source claim, and wait for host return and reconcile.

reasonCodes.meaning: After clean source release no complete compatible target solution exists.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Keep the VM stopped and choose another online qualified target or capacity.

reasonCodes.meaning: The host has unresolved old runs, owners, grants, processes, or quarantine records.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Complete reconcile before admitting the host to any candidate pool.

reasonCodes.meaning: The caller or plan lacks the authority required to change a quarantine generation.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Use the privileged approved remediation workflow.

reasonCodes.meaning: Live migration is outside the DirectPath V3 capability boundary.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Use planned cold relocation with both hosts online.

reasonCodes.meaning: VM snapshot is unsupported while DirectPath configuration is present.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Remove DirectPath through a clean powered-off workflow if snapshot is required.

reasonCodes.meaning: Suspend/resume is unsupported for a DirectPath VM.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Use supported power-off/power-on lifecycle.

reasonCodes.meaning: Fault Tolerance is outside the DirectPath V3 boundary.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Use a workload design that does not require FT for this VM.

reasonCodes.meaning: Runtime PCI add, delete, or Dynamic backing replacement is unsupported.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Power off and use the managed configuration/start path.

reasonCodes.meaning: A raw QEMU, QMP, sysfs, or VFIO path attempted to bypass the managed admission transaction.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Disable the bypass and use the sealed managed launcher path.

reasonCodes.meaning: Required append-only audit persistence failed for a mutation.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Fail the mutation or retain its nonterminal claim until audit durability is restored.

reasonCodes.meaning: A commit or release evidence bundle lacks a required artifact identity or hash.
reasonCodes.operatorAction: Do not advance the release/qualification claim; collect the missing artifact.

rules: Every behavior-changing value is versioned, hashed into policy/profile/plan provenance, and audited.
A missing safety setting uses the fail-closed default, never an auto-detected permissive fallback.
Backend, firmware, QEMU, kernel, solver, topology, and lifecycle changes invalidate affected qualification until re-verification.
Secrets and deployment addresses are target configuration, not portable contract values.

settings.meaning: Only one current controller generation advances DirectPath FSMs.
Current product path is an exact qualified Legacy VFIO TYPE1 adapter.
A requested backend never falls back at runtime.
No-IOMMU cannot satisfy per-device DMA isolation.

settings.constraint: Greater than zero and less than the platform-specific validated control-loop bound.
settings.meaning: Age is an additional freshness gate and never replaces epoch/hash comparison.

settings.constraint: Must cover the largest qualified topology while bounding nonconvergent input.
settings.meaning: Closure overflow is a denial, not a truncated bundle.

settings.constraint: Positive bounded duration with no greedy fallback.
settings.meaning: Timeout returns MMIO_PLANNER_TIMEOUT or PROFILE_NO_GLOBAL_SOLUTION without partial output.
Expiry may trigger reconciliation but can never free, revoke, or reassign a physical bundle.

settings.constraint: Versioned profile-specific read/control allowlist; excludes device_add, device_del, migration, and topology-changing properties.
settings.meaning: Production QMP exposes only managed lifecycle and observation commands.

settings.constraint: Exact digest required by compatibility profile.
settings.meaning: Binary drift cannot inherit prior qualification.

settings.constraint: Exact OVMF or SeaBIOS digest required by compatibility profile.
settings.meaning: Firmware source alone is insufficient; the shipped digest is the profile input.

settings.constraint: One of x86 q35/i440fx with UEFI/SeaBIOS or ARM virt with UEFI, on an exact platform line.
settings.meaning: Machine, firmware, memory, MMIO, device-count, ROM, IRQ, and guest ABI rules are one unit.
A booted or reconnected host is excluded from candidate pools until reconcile completes.
No BMC, power fencing, source-loss takeover, or automatic host-failure restart.
deviceUid, BDF, assignmentId, and evidence hashes belong in controlled logs/audit, not public metric labels.

settings.constraint: Exact digest of the offline-provisioned DirectPath Ed25519 root public-key set; change requires a separately authorized trust migration and rollback-anchor update.
settings.meaning: A key advertised by a database/catalog is never trusted unless its key-ring root signatures chain to this provisioned digest.

steps.rollback: Deny new power-on; reconcile and cleanly release existing assignments; never delete leases.

Planner purity, full-group live apply/rollback, deferred intent, early-boot claim, and post-boot identity/owner readback.
Exact identity, atomic lease, attach, repeated physical reuse, injected partial failures, reset uncertainty, rollback, and quarantine.
Exact planner, firmware/machine matrix, BAR/bridge/MMIO/RMRR/device-count boundary, timeout denial, and observed-plan match.

Versioned PCI error capability and body read/write policy; independently observed status deposition, message routing, bounded logs, lifecycle clear/reuse and recovery; synthetic reference evidence is separated from exact-device physical qualification.
API, scheduler, launcher, QMP, concurrent bypass, and backend denial without assignment-state mutation.
Selector normalization, exact and deterministic whole solve, nonoverlap, atomic reserve, epoch conflict recompute, assignedId lifetime, and shared Static recovery core.
Both-online handshake, source stop and complete clean-release receipt, target re-solve/new assignedId, source-loss no-takeover, and target exhaustion.
Legacy current adapter is exact and fail-closed; every future cdev profile independently proves the same control semantics and its fd/ioctl ownership.
Consumer GPU, professional GPU, HBA, and accelerator are evaluated by technical traits and exact errata/profile evidence rather than wildcard class support.
Controller/agent/QEMU/store fault injection, stale-mutation denial, retained claims, correlated audit, artifact hashes, and fail-closed release evaluation.

vmwareParityObligations.portableRequirement: IOMMU, physical isolation, dependency, reset, owner, and policy facts produce conservative capability and stable reasons on every Qman platform.
Configured intent and effective owner remain distinct across live, deferred, reboot, and failure states.
A bundle cannot remain partially activated, and stale boot identity cannot silently become the effective passthrough owner.
Static backing is stable, exclusive, identity checked, and released before reuse.
Selectors, complete-bundle solving, all-or-nothing reservation, runtime-only assignedId, and release-before-retry share the Static transaction core.
Firmware, machine profile, BAR/MMIO, reserved ranges, and full-memory requirements are versioned admission inputs with post-start verification.
PCI error capability, status deposition, message routing, guest writes, bounded observability, lifecycle cleanup and recovery are separate versioned policy surfaces; one cannot prove another.
Q35/i440fx/virt, OVMF/SeaBIOS, exact bridge topology, and exact BAR addresses may differ from VMware if the Qman guest ABI is versioned and its admission result is equivalent.
Old guest DMA and IRQ state is unreachable after release; reset uncertainty retains the whole bundle and blocks reuse.
The in-scope Qman API, scheduler, launcher, and runtime control paths reject snapshot, suspend/resume, and live migration for DirectPath VMs.
Both hosts remain online and cooperative; source stop, assignedId clear, DMA/IRQ teardown, reset/owner readback, and durable run revocation precede target attach and re-solve.

The capability engine is generic and evaluates consumer GPU, professional GPU, HBA, and accelerator traits plus conservative errata. Production SUPPORTED admission nevertheless requires an exact signed QualificationRecord key and SupportedCatalog digest for the complete platform/device/firmware/guest/workload profile; trait families are taxonomy and test coverage, never wildcard support.

Qman does not copy VMware catalog contents, naming, or format. It maintains its own exact signed QualificationRecord/SupportedCatalog allow entries, may present them grouped by type/trait, and keeps technically attachable but noncatalog devices unsupported.
Legacy and modern VFIO backends use one Qman control-plane contract; VMware private implementation is not a parity target.
Operator-visible owner, VM, source/target host, device, assignedId, action, result, and evidence identity remain correlated across Static, Dynamic, and cold relocation.
An unreachable or failed source host is never treated as cleanly released; Qman does not restart the VM elsewhere and does not integrate BMC or power fencing.
Qman does not provide FT for DirectPath VMs; absence of a local VMware FT run is not a V3 blocker.
Qman does not provide fixed or Dynamic runtime PCI hotplug; all Qman mutation paths must reject it.

mappingSurface.verificationMatrixRule: The generator emits exactly one ordered, hash-bound row for every derived mapping item. TEST is self-covered; PARITY uses its declared tests; PORT uses acceptance Tech Story intersection; OPERATION inherits its owner PORT; TRANSITION unions its operations and adds TEST-CRASH-RECONCILE-AUDIT when any operation is side-effecting; STATE_MACHINE unions its transitions; REASON unions listing operations; CAS_RULE unions referencing transitions; EQUIVALENCE uses TEST-DYNAMIC; ENTITY uses its FSM when present; all other kinds and every empty derivation conservatively require all obligations. requiredCaseIds is the exact ordered union of those obligations and every row requires all eight scenario oracle classes. requirementDigest is SHA-256(CANONICAL-JSON-V1(row without requirementDigest)). A target mapping binds this digest by const; scenario self-claims cannot reduce or expand it.
mappingSurface.completionRule: TARGET_CODE_MAPPED is true only when every derived item exists exactly once and is BOUND to exact target symbols, an explicitly approved CONFLICT, or an authority-backed DEFERRED item on FUTURE_SEPARATELY_QUALIFIED; the target repository commit is pinned and no item remains UNMAPPED.
mappingSurface.implementationRule: PRODUCT_IMPLEMENTED is true only when every CURRENT_RELEASE_REQUIRED mapping is BOUND and VERIFIED by target tests, with no conflict. A FUTURE_SEPARATELY_QUALIFIED item may remain DEFERRED without weakening the current Legacy release. QUALIFIED additionally requires exact physical E4 profile evidence; enabling a deferred track requires a new profile, mapping, implementation, qualification, and release approval.
